# Locksmith

> Hardware biometric secrets vault, sovereign SPIFFE CA, and MCP server for AI agents backed by Touch ID, Windows Hello, and TPM2.

## Core Capabilities
- Native Hardware Biometrics: Bridges developer and agent workflows with Apple Secure Enclave (Touch ID / Apple Watch), Windows Hello, and Linux TPM2/Secret Service.
- Sovereign SPIFFE CA & Workload API: Issues short-lived X.509 SVIDs (`spiffe://bonjoski/agent/...`) for mTLS mutual authentication between autonomous agents and proxies.
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server: Provides structured `get_secret` and `list_secrets` tools for Claude, Antigravity, and Cursor with prompt-time biometric verification.
- Ephemeral Execution Injection: CyberArk Summon provider (`summon-locksmith`) and `locksmith run` inject secrets into process environments without disk persistence.
- In-Memory Secret Slicing: Fragments secrets into non-contiguous memory slices with automatic memory zeroization on lease expiration.
- Multi-Agent Biometric Amortization: Caches biometric confirmation leases (300s window) with token burst limits across concurrent subagent loops.

## CLI Usage
- `locksmith add <KEY>`: Encrypts and stores secret in the platform enclave.
- `locksmith get <KEY>`: Prompts for biometric unlock and outputs secret value.
- `locksmith list`: Lists stored secret keys (values redacted).
- `locksmith run --secret <KEY> -- <command>`: Executes command with ephemeral secret injected.
- `locksmith spiffe server`: Launches the SPIFFE Workload API server.
- `locksmith spiffe mint --spiffe-id <ID>`: Mints an attested X.509 SVID certificate.
- `locksmith mcp`: Launches stdio Model Context Protocol server.
- `locksmith slice --key <KEY>`: Fragment secret into sliced in-memory buffers.
- `locksmith doctor`: Probes hardware enclaves and codesigning entitlements.

## Key Sockets & Files
- Control Socket: `~/.locksmith/locksmith.sock`
- SPIFFE Socket: `~/.locksmith/spiffe.sock`
- Documentation: README.md & AGENTS.md
